newsitem.title: TURKEY: Private Turkish hospital floats part capital. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Private Turkish hospital floats part capital. [CORRECTED 13:30 GMT]

text.p: Turkey's private hospital Sevgi Ozel Saglik Hizmetleri A.S. floated part of its share capital on Thursday in a two-day public offer, the first time a health institution has gone on the market.
For each 1,000 lira nominal-valued share, the fixed offer price is 8,950 lira, the company said in newspaper circulars.
Sevgi is offering 125 billion lira of new shares and 35 billion lira of old shares to the public when raising its capital to 825 billion lira from 700 billion.
The offer is managed by a consortium led by Global Securities and including six other brokerages as members.

The Ankara-based hospital's net profits jumped to 239 billion lira and net sales to 1.28 (corrects figure from 2.28) trillion lira in 1996 from 61.9 billion and 531.9 billion, respectively the previous year.
Its total assets surged to 1.55 trillion lira last year, from 663.4 billion in 1995. Total sales reached to 1.3 trillion lira when compared to 532 billion lira in the same period.
Of the total 160 billion lira share offer, 104 billion lira was allocated to foreign investors, eight billion to domestic investment funds and trusts and the rest to domestic individual investors.
Sevgi Hospital belongs to Orhan Ozcanl who is also the owner of Sevgi Holding.
The circular said income from the public offer would be used to finance a new hospital building project in Ankara.
